correctness.rationale: For ordinary acyclic path algebra with a arrows 1->2 and b arrows 2->3, two-sided radical ideals split under vertex Peirce projectors into U<=V, Z<=W and T<=V⊗W; closure iff U⊗W+V⊗Z<=T. Codimension (a-u)(b-z) yields Gaussian subspace factor. Because only V·W survives, IK=U_I⊗Z_K. For nonzero rectangular tensors the two contraction supports recover U and Z uniquely; all nonrectangle targets have zero fiber. Thus F(0)=N(A0+B0)-A0B0 and F(U⊗Z)=A_u B_z, and equality of products gives the presented commuting-pair formula. Every positive product dimension is uv; for a=b=2, dim 3 is excluded. Independently enumerated all F2 radical ideals and actual products for (a,b)=(1,1),(2,1),(1,2), yielding (N,F0,C)=(5,21,19) and (17,234,199), and exact Gaussian formulas for (2,2,2)=(124,13695,12682). These finite checks do not establish arbitrary q; the field-linear Peirce/tensor proof does.
residual_risks: Older general noncommutative quiver ideal-semigroup or subspace-incidence results may imply these formulas.
Finite direct field enumeration was performed only over F2, while unrestricted proof uses Peirce decomposition for any prime power.

originality.rationale: Rangaswamy 2016 analyzes Leavitt path algebras where ghost arrows and CK relations radically change ideal multiplication, which is commutative there. Catoiu–Chin–Krop provide general finite-dimensional ideal methods but the inspected text did not include complete ordered radical product fibers for this quiver. The same-day Resultary radical-square-zero quiver theorem has J²=0, while here J²=V⊗W≠0 and multiplication is visibly noncommutative. A four-vertex multiarrow commuting-element result is likewise distinct from ideal multiplication.
